## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duṭṭhadosa Sikkhāpada* constitutes the eighth rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. According to the rule, a monk who, motivated by anger and malice, makes an unfounded accusation against another monk concerning an offense entailing expulsion (*pārājika*) is subject to formal suspension (*saṅghādisesa*). The rule's origin story centers on the figure of Dabba the Mallian (*Dabba Mallaputta*), a venerable monk who attained arahantship at the age of seven and served the saṅgha by assigning lodgings and apportioning meals.

 Complete translations into modern languages include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
